evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 形義通解; 甲骨、金文、簡帛字例; 《說文》; 《廣韻》
evidence.text: The entry says the oracle-bone and bronze graph resembles two hands facing the same direction, sometimes joined, suggesting friendliness, and explicitly assigns 又 a phonetic role as well. It reports oracle-bone contexts for a personal name and for 侑 in sacrifice; bronze contexts for friends, friendly relations, associates, and officials; and a Mawangdui Laozi A use 友弱勝強 parallel to B 柔弱勝強. The page gives no absolute dates for these individual witnesses, so the reported contexts do not establish a semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：友

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: Lists oracle-bone, bronze (including inscription 集成04178), Chu manuscript, and small-seal forms. Its interpretation identifies two 又 (hands) as semantic elements and says the small-seal 又 forms were arranged vertically. This supports a two-hands analysis, but not a claim that cooperation was necessarily the historically intended scene. The page states All Rights Reserved.
evidence.title: 漢字「友」：字形演變

The dossier reports it as a modern Shuowen seal-style vector and public domain, but the page could not be opened in this run and the exact imageinfo API request was inaccessible. The direct original image URL from a local manifest is only a lead and was not independently verified here, so this file is not proposed as a glyph asset.

search_audit.query: 友 字形演變 甲骨 金文 又 形聲 漢語多功能字庫; site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File: 友-seal.svg; 友 小學堂 字形演變 CC0
search_audit.outcome: Search located CUHK and Academia Sinica character records, the exact Commons file description, and Xiaoxuetang rights notice. Opened and inspected the CUHK and Academia Sinica pages and rights notice. Commons file page returned a cache miss; exact MediaWiki imageinfo API request was inaccessible.

gaps: The two 又 forms have reported semantic roles as hands; CUHK also assigns 又 a phonetic role. The exact function of each repeated shape remains unresolved. The supplied Baxter–Sagart local rows record 又 as *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s (MC hjuwH) and 友 as *[ɢ]ʷəʔ (MC hjuwX), but their upstream PDF was inaccessible in this run; those local readings are not newly verified external evidence.

The earliest reported contexts are oracle-bone personal-name and sacrificial 侑 uses, but neither the absolute dates of the cited witnesses nor priority between those contexts is established by the inspected page. Bronze friend/associate uses and the Mawangdui whole-graph spelling 友 for 柔 are separately reported; no continuous semantic chain or independent sound basis for the borrowing is established.

No glyph image is selected. Commons file page and API could not be inspected, and no exact Xiaoxuetang form/image record was obtained. Local image paths and URLs are leads only, not verified image provenance or reuse permissions.

limitations.text: The sources report early two-hand forms and later vertical small-seal arrangement, but no image with verified identity, direct image URL, and reuse provenance was established in this run. Commons description and exact imageinfo lookups failed; the Xiaoxuetang rights notice was verified, but no exact character-specific image candidate was retrieved.
